text_blocks.snippet: Early symptoms of type 2 diabetes develop slowly and include increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue. Many people do not notice these mild signs for years.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: More thirst and bathroom trips: Your kidneys work hard to remove extra sugar. This pulls water from your body, making you pee a lot and feel very thirsty.
Extreme tiredness: Your cells cannot use blood sugar for energy. This lack of fuel leaves you feeling weak and exhausted.
Constant hunger: Your body fails to get energy from food. You may feel hungry soon after eating a full meal.
Blurry vision: High sugar levels change fluid in your eyes. Your eye lenses swell and lose focus.
Slow-healing cuts: High sugar harms your blood flow and nerves. Small scrapes or sores take a long time to heal.
Frequent infections: Extra sugar helps germs grow. You might get more skin, bladder, or yeast infections.
Tingling hands or feet: High sugar can damage your nerves. You might feel a numb or prickling sensation in your limbs.
Dark skin patches: Dark, velvety skin on your neck or armpits can show insulin resistance (when your body's cells do not respond well to insulin).

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more about these signs through the Mayo Clinic or the CDC. A simple blood test from a doctor is the only way to confirm if you have diabetes.
